summary: A 1930s Aermotor MC-39 cab retired from Forest Service duty in Montana in 1995, restored, and re-erected in 2023 as a park feature in Spring, Texas.

access.note: Stands in Cypress Creek Park, a Timber Lane Utility District park open to the public; whether the tower itself can be climbed is not documented in available sources.

events.note: Aermotor MC-39 cab decommissioned by the U.S. Forest Service in western Montana after about 60 years of service
Restored by Davanna LLC (Bloomingdale, NY) and reconstructed in Cypress Creek Park, Spring, Texas
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, January 2, 2026, as US 1811, TX 5

sources.title: Texas lookout list ("Spring (Relocated from MT)", Harris County)

notes_for_editor: No newspaper, NRHP, or forest-history coverage found specific to this tower; it is recent (built 2023, NHLR-registered Jan 2026) so that may simply not exist yet. The NHLR nominator, Alfred Francis Gessel, shares a surname with a contact address once suspected on the Timber Lane Utility District site, raising a guess that he may be a district official involved in bringing the tower to the park — but this was never sourced (the district-facilities page carries no contact names or emails) and has been dropped from the story entirely rather than left as insinuation. Climbability and drive-up access are unconfirmed; the park's own page references a 'Fire Tower Flyer' that was not reachable in this research. One correction applied: the NHLR elevation figure (113 ft / 34 m) is not labeled by the register as site elevation vs. structure height, so the story no longer asserts which it is. The district-facilities source was dropped (it supported neither the Fire Tower Flyer mention, which is on the parks-and-trails page, nor the contact-name claim, which isn't on the site at all); the FFLA citation is renumbered [^3] accordingly.
